_meta.denominator: team targets/air yards summed over GAMES PLAYED, never the full season

pairs_with.rule: BOTH vintages render, always. The prior season is never overwritten and the current one never silently replaces it.

trend_rules.both_sides: `trend` is the PASSING side, `trend_car` the RUSHING side. A back can be flat in one and moving in the other — RJ Harvey 2025 reads stable on target share while his touches doubled. Read both for RBs.
trend_rules.insufficient: means not enough games to split, NOT a flat role. Never render it as stable.
trend_rules.rank: 1 — role/opportunity CHANGE, which outranks the season aggregate sitting beside it
trend_rules.windows: calendar (W1-9 vs W10-18) only on a complete season, otherwise halves of the weeks covered. The two are different measurements and never comparable.

rules.bar: 1 SD of the observed shift distribution, derived per metric from this run. It is WIDE early, because a two game sample is noisy, and narrows on its own as games accumulate. Nothing here is hand-typed.
rules.changed_team: the prior was earned on another offence. The shift is real and nothing may render it without naming the team it came from.
rules.decisions_only: this file carries no yards, no touchdowns and no efficiency, so every shift it can report is a change in what a coaching staff DID. What happened afterwards is not here by construction.
rules.method: BOTH seasons are computed by THIS builder. Never diff against player_metrics_2025.json - its shares use a season-level team denominator, so every mid-season mover reads as a fake role change.
rules.moved_null: means NOT YET MEASURABLE, never 'did not move'. Rendering the two the same way turns an unknown into a finding.
rules.no_pair: a player absent from this block has no prior-season row - a rookie, or someone under the game gate. That is an absent baseline, NOT a gate he failed.
